faqs.question: What is the difference between the DSC200 and DSC600?
faqs.answer: Both share the NEXTA platform and the −150 to 725 °C range. The DSC600 adds three thermocouples to the centric sensor for a 3 s time constant, 0.05 µW noise and 0.1 µW sensitivity — ideal for resolving overlapping or weak transitions. The DSC200 is a 6.5 s centric sensor (0.1 µW noise, 0.2 µW sensitivity) tuned for routine and general research.

faqs.question: What temperature range can it cover?
faqs.answer: −150 °C to 725 °C. The low end depends on the cooling accessory: an electric cooler for moderate sub-ambient work, or an intracooler to reach −150 °C.

faqs.question: Is Real View standard?
faqs.answer: Real View is an option on both models. The camera synchronises sample video with the thermogram; a Polarized Micro unit (20 MP, 50× zoom, 1.2 µm) is available for crystal observation.

faqs.question: Are the software modules extra?
faqs.answer: No. All core analysis modules are supplied as standard. The Data I/O package (barcode, 5000-sample library, CSV/Excel export) is an optional add-on.

faqs.question: Can it do photo-DSC / UV-cure studies?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the PDC-8 (Hg-Xe, 240–550 nm, up to 500 mW/cm²) or PDC-8LED (365/385/395/405 nm, 150 mW/cm²) photochemical calorimeter accessory.

sections.title: 01 — Product Information
body: Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) measures the difference in heat flow between a sample and an inert reference as both follow a controlled temperature program. The resulting thermogram reveals melting, crystallisation, glass transition, curing, oxidation and other events — each with its characteristic temperature and enthalpy. The NEXTA DSC uses a heat-flux design with a highly symmetric sensor to keep baselines flat and transitions sharp.

Two models share the same platform so you can match performance to your work. The DSC200 is a centric heat-flux sensor tuned for routine and general research with a 6.5 s time constant. The DSC600 adds three thermocouples to the centric sensor for the fastest response (3 s time constant) and the lowest noise, resolving closely spaced events that a standard sensor would blur together.
Value in one line: stable baselines, class-leading sensitivity, Real View observation and software that makes method setup and reporting effortless — all backed by Inkarp service in India.

faqs.question: What does 'simultaneous' TG-DSC mean?
faqs.answer: The instrument measures mass change (TG) and heat flow (DSC) from the same sample at the same time, under one atmosphere and one temperature program. This lets you link every mass loss directly to its thermal event — something separate TG and DSC runs cannot do unambiguously.

faqs.question: Which model should I choose?
faqs.answer: STA200 reaches 1,100 °C for general TG-DSC; STA200RV reaches 1,000 °C with Real View included for colour and visual-change studies; STA300 reaches 1,500 °C for ceramics, metals and high-temperature inorganics.

faqs.question: How stable is the balance?
faqs.answer: The horizontal differential balance holds baseline drift and stability below 10 µg, with temperature precision ±0.07 °C and accuracy ±0.2 °C.

faqs.question: Can I control the atmosphere?
faqs.answer: Yes. Integrated mass-flow control with up to four controllers lets you run inert or reactive gases and switch mid-run — for example inert pyrolysis followed by an air burn for carbon-black analysis.

faqs.question: What is Real View?
faqs.answer: A camera that records the sample during the run and links each image to the curve by timestamp, with colour quantification in LAB, CMYK and RGB. It is standard on the STA200RV and optional on the STA200 and STA300.

faqs.question: Is the software extra?
faqs.answer: No. All software modules are included at no extra cost — guidance mode, automated analysis, data management and reporting. The Cp (specific heat) module is an option.

faqs.question: Which standards are built in?
faqs.answer: ASTM E1269, E1641-16, E794-06, E793-06 and ISO 11357-2/3/4, ISO 11358-3, ISO 22768, with conformance to ISO/ASTM/DIN/JIS generally.

sections.title: 01 — Product Information
body: Simultaneous Thermal Analysis (STA) measures thermogravimetry (TG — mass versus temperature) and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC — heat flow versus temperature) at the same time on the same specimen. Because both signals come from one sample under one atmosphere and one temperature program, you can correlate a mass loss directly with its thermal event — for example confirming that an endotherm is dehydration rather than melting, or that an exotherm is oxidation of a specific component.

The NEXTA STA uses a horizontal differential balance for an exceptionally stable baseline (drift and stability < 10 µg) and an innovative furnace design for fast, uniform heating. Choose the model by the top temperature your work needs: STA200 to 1,100 °C, STA200RV (Real View ready) to 1,000 °C, or STA300 to 1,500 °C for ceramics, metals and high-temperature inorganics.
Value in one line: one sample, two measurements, a rock-steady balance and all software included — backed by Inkarp service across India.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the TMA7100 and TMA7300?
faqs.answer: The TMA7100 covers −170 °C to 600 °C with quartz or metal sample systems and offers expansion, penetration and tension modes. The TMA7300 extends expansion measurement to 1,500 °C with an alumina system for ceramics, metals and high-temperature inorganics. Both share ±5 mm range, 0.01 µm sensitivity, ±5.8 N load and 0.01–100 °C/min scan rates.

faqs.question: How sensitive is the displacement measurement?
faqs.answer: 0.01 µm, with ultra-low noise — fine enough to resolve the small expansion of low-CTE ceramics, glass, laminates and thin films.

faqs.question: What can TMA measure?
faqs.answer: Coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE), softening and penetration temperature, dimensional change at the glass transition, and — through NEXTA software — creep and stress relaxation.

faqs.question: What load can it apply?
faqs.answer: Up to ±5.8 N, set through the software to suit expansion, penetration or tension measurements.

faqs.question: What cooling is available?
faqs.answer: Liquid-nitrogen cooling (with an optimised furnace that cuts LN₂ use by about 30 %), plus air and electrical cooling depending on the temperature range required.

faqs.question: What probes and accessories are offered?
faqs.answer: Seven optional measurement probes, plus swelling, vacuum, volume-expansion and curing accessories, extend the range of measurements.

faqs.question: Which standards are built in?
faqs.answer: ASTM E1269, E1641-16, E794-06, E793-06 and ISO 11357-2/3/4, ISO 11358-3, ISO 22768, with conformance to ISO/ASTM/DIN/JIS generally.

sections.title: 01 — Product Information
body: Thermomechanical Analysis (TMA) measures how the dimensions of a material change with temperature under a defined load. A probe rests on the sample and tracks its length as the furnace follows a temperature program; the result is the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE), softening point, glass-transition-related dimensional change, and — with the right probe and load — penetration, creep and stress relaxation. TMA is the method of choice when dimensional stability is the engineering question.

The TMA7000 series pairs a high-sensitivity 0.01 µm displacement system with ultra-low noise, so even the tiny expansion of low-CTE ceramics, glass and electronic laminates is clearly resolved. The TMA7100 covers −170 °C to 600 °C with quartz or metal sample cylinders and three deformation modes; the TMA7300 extends expansion measurement to 1,500 °C with an alumina system for ceramics and high-temperature inorganics.
Value in one line: sub-micron dimensional measurement from cryogenic to 1,500 °C, with NEXTA software and Inkarp service across India.

faqs.answer: Up to 20 N, with a fine 5×10⁻⁶ N applied-force resolution. This range lets one instrument test very stiff composites and very soft elastomers or gels.

faqs.answer: −150 °C with liquid-nitrogen cooling, −100 °C with electric gas cooling, or room temperature with air cooling — all up to 600 °C.

faqs.question: What deformation modes are available?
faqs.answer: Tension and dual/single cantilever as standard, plus optional 3-point bending, compression, shear and film shear — covering a 10³ to 10¹³·⁵ Pa modulus range.

faqs.question: Is master-curve (TTS) analysis included?

sections.title: 01 — Product Information
body: Dynamic Mechanical Analysis (DMA) applies a small oscillating force to a sample and measures the resulting deformation. From the amplitude and phase of the response the instrument derives the storage modulus (E′ — elastic stiffness), loss modulus (E″ — viscous dissipation) and loss tangent (tan δ — damping). Running these while scanning temperature or frequency exposes the glass transition, secondary relaxations, cure, softening and the frequency dependence of mechanical properties.

The NEXTA DMA200 uses an LVDT displacement sensor and a spring-mounted drive shaft, so no compressed-air supply is needed. A 20 N maximum force combined with 5×10⁻⁶ N force resolution lets one instrument span from rigid carbon-fibre laminates to soft gels. The Real View camera records the sample throughout the run, linking every image to the curve by timestamp.
Value in one line: one analyzer for stiff and soft materials, with guided method setup, standard TTS/master-curve analysis and Inkarp service across India.
